issues.on_page: Other: General 41,283, Keno 16,458, Street 8,025, CDBG Housing Rehab 17,706 = 83,472
issues.issue: The report explains most of this line. The Keno column's 16,458 is 'Lottery proceeds' (p3), so it fits keno/lottery. General's 41,283 includes Donations/contributions 16,650 (p15). CDBG's 17,706 is the Economic Development operating grant (p2). The rest, 32,658 = 'Other miscellaneous revenues' (p3), is unexplained. No single category is over half, so 'other' with review is defensible, but a per-column split (keno/lottery 16,458) would be more accurate. The review note says the remainder is unexplained but does not mention the donations.

issues.on_page: Rural Fire Department 55,532 (Fire column, under Intergovernmental revenues)
issues.issue: Under the receipt rules, rural fire contracts are charges for services/fees. The report lists this under intergovernmental, and p2 counts it as an operating grant (Public Health and Safety 76,559 = 21,027 + 55,532), so either category is defensible.
Nebraska mutual finance assistance is paid by the state, so 'other state aid' may fit better.

issues.on_page: Statement of Receipts, Disbursements and Changes in Fund Balances - Budget and Actual - All Fund Types (one combined 'General All-Purpose Fund' column, including proprietary)
issues.issue: Leaving it out avoids double counting the General Fund. The cost is that Street, Keno, CDBG, ARPA, Debt Service and the utility funds have no budget detail. The schedule prints one combined column, so it can't be split by fund. This is a defensible judgment call.
